title: Isolation of Phytopathogenic Fungi
author: Daisy Perez-Brito
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sgsebwe

steps.title: Prepare diseased plant tissues
steps.instruction: Cut diseased plant tissues from the advanced margin of lesions into small pieces (5 × 5 mm) using a scalpel.

steps.title: Disinfect plant tissues
steps.instruction: Disinfect the tissue pieces by immersing them in a 3% NaOCl solution.

steps.title: Rinse tissues
steps.instruction: Rinse the disinfected pieces with sterile distilled water three times.

steps.title: Initial fungal isolation
steps.instruction: Transfer each small piece onto a 90 x 15 mm Petri Dish containing Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) medium.

steps.title: First incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at room temperature (25°C) for 7 days.

steps.title: Isolate mycelial segments
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, cut a mycelial segment of approximately 5 x 5 mm from the edge of each fungi colony.

steps.title: Transfer to water-agar
steps.instruction: Transfer each small mycelial piece onto a 90 x 15 mm Petri dish containing 2% water-agar medium.

steps.title: Second incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at room temperature (25°C) for 5 days.

steps.title: Isolate single hyphae tip
steps.instruction: Observe the fungal colony under a stereo microscope and use a 29 gauge insulin syringe needle to cut one hyphae tip.

steps.title: Final transfer to PDA
steps.instruction: Transfer the isolated hyphae tip onto a 90 x 15 mm Petri Dish containing Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) medium.

steps.title: Final incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at room temperature (25°C) for 7 days.
